name: OLIX
summary: OLIX is a UK-based AI-chip startup developing specialised inference hardware linked by a photonic interconnect.
overview: OLIX is developing custom AI inference chips and a photonic interconnect intended to support high-performance AI systems. In August 2026, it announced a $312 million Series B at a $3.3 billion valuation to support first-rack delivery and custom-silicon execution.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: OLIX announced a $312 million Series B at a $3.3 billion valuation.

bull_case: If OLIX can execute on silicon, interconnect, and supply-chain commitments, specialised inference hardware could offer a differentiated route into AI infrastructure.
bear_case: Semiconductor development is capital intensive, technically risky, and dominated by well-funded incumbents with established software ecosystems.
latest_round: August 2026 Series B: $312M at a $3.3B valuation
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: A UK AI-chip company developing specialised inference hardware and photonic interconnects.
company: OLIX is developing a custom silicon platform for AI inference, including specialised chips connected through a photonic interconnect. The company says the architecture is intended to support demanding AI workloads as it moves toward first racks.

In August 2026, OLIX announced a $312 million Series B at a $3.3 billion valuation, following a February fundraise reported at a $1 billion valuation. The financing is intended to support silicon development, manufacturing commitments, and delivery to customers.
intelligence.why_it_matters: AI inference is drawing investment beyond the leading GPU supply chain. OLIX is a high-risk, high-capital example of a private company trying to build an alternative hardware stack.

changed.text: OLIX announced a $312M Series B at a $3.3B valuation.

takeaways: The August 2026 Series B set a $3.3B valuation benchmark.
Product delivery and manufacturing execution are the key near-term milestones.
The company faces formidable semiconductor and platform competition.
